story.head: The Capitals can’t afford to take penalties
paras: The Capitals have won three straight, while the Stars (7-5-1) lost 5-2 to Montréal on Thursday. Going in, the Stars are fourth in the Central (tied for 16th in the NHL) and the Capitals third in the Metropolitan (tied for 13th).
The Stars’ record (.577) is about what their chances are worth. The Capitals’ record (.667) is running ahead of what their chances are worth (.575), largely thanks to their goaltending.

The Stars play slow, tight games (lowest) and take more penalties than they draw (31st). They also block more shots than anyone (1st), and the Capitals’ knack for getting shots through meets a team that blocks a lot. Dallas has allowed 2.23 goals a game, the fewest in the league. The Caps get the league’s best looks (1st) and have had some of the best goaltending in the league (3rd). They also have a leaky penalty kill (27th), so the Stars’ power play (2nd) could do real damage when they’re shorthanded.

Mikko Rantanen (6 G / 10 A / 16 P in 13 GP) leads the Stars in scoring, with eight points in his last five games. Jason Robertson (5 G / 8 A / 13 P in 13 GP) isn’t far behind. Alex Tuch (10 G / 2 A / 12 P in 12 GP) is tied for the Capitals’ scoring lead. Dylan Strome (3 G / 9 A / 12 P in 12 GP) shares it, with seven points in his last five games.
Jake Oettinger (6-3-1 / .917 SV% in 10 GS) has been terrific for Dallas and will likely start. Logan Thompson (5-3-0 / .903 SV% in 8 GS) is in line to start for Washington.
At home, Spencer Carbery likes to send Protas, Dubois and Wilson out against the other team’s top line, so watch for them against Steel, Johnston and Rantanen.

items.text: The Stars have been without Esa Lindell since Oct 17, and have had to make do without Matt Duchene all season.
Roope Hintz has a point in five straight games against Washington.
The Capitals have been without Rasmus Sandin for several games.
Tom Wilson has one goal on chances worth about 3.7 goals, well below what his finishing usually turns chances into. If the chances keep coming, so should the goals.
